distinctions_drawn: Human psychological complexity vs. computational syntax generation
explicit_definitions_given: Syntax: formal, local, physical, rule-governed symbol manipulation
Semantics: relation between symbols and world; reference, truth, extension
Intensionality: mode of presentation; failure of substitutivity salva veritate

dialectical_engagement.objection_handling: Two objections anticipated and rebutted: distributed systems reply and human proliferation reply
objections_raised: Modern neural networks have high-dimensional semantic geometries, not static symbols
Humans also produce multiple interpretations of ambiguous stimuli

method_and_evidence.evidence_type: Conceptual analysis, thought experiment, counterexample, appeal to intuitions about meaning and consciousness

philosophical_orientation.thematic_focus: Machine understanding, intensionality, semantic determinacy, limits of formalism

structural_organization.structure_type: Dialectical essay with numbered sections and subheadings

summary_of_core_decisions: The text uses a modified Chinese Room thought experiment—the Rorschach Room—to argue that a multilingual syntactic engine producing contradictory interpretations of ambiguous stimuli cannot possess intensional states. It frames a dilemma: either syntax is insufficient for semantics, or machine understanding is reduced to absurdity. It rejects the second horn and embraces the first, defending the conclusion against functionalist and human-analogy objections.
